# Real-`.xlsm` slot for the safe-round-trip milestone

`tests/xlsx_roundtrip.rs`'s three tests (`xlsm_roundtrip_preserves_vba_project_and_declares_macro_enabled_content_types`,
`xlsx_roundtrip_passes_through_unknown_parts_without_macro_content_type`,
`xlsm_roundtrip_in_place_save_preserves_vba_project`) verify unknown-OOXML-part
passthrough and `xl/vbaProject.bin` preservation against a fixture built
**in-test**, via `zip::write::ZipWriter` (the same dependency `save_xlsx_impl`
itself uses) — not a committed binary file.

Two reasons, not one:
- No real Microsoft-Excel-authored `.xlsm` exists anywhere in this repo today
  (confirmed by a full-repo search before this milestone started).
- Even once one exists, a hand-built Rust fixture is more reviewable as source
  than an opaque committed binary blob, and the `xl/vbaProject.bin` stand-in
  needs to be a deterministic, non-trivial (not all-zero) byte pattern so a
  writer bug that truncates or zeroes the part is actually caught by byte
  equality — something a real compiled VBA project's binary would also do,
  incidentally, but doesn't need real Excel to produce.

**This directory is the slot for the real thing when it becomes available.**
This mirrors the existing, already-proven precedent at
`tests/fixtures/e2e/README.md` (`source.xlsx`/`source.ods`, generated by a real
office suite rather than hand-built or SheetJS-generated) — "synthetic
reasoning first, real-producer file added later."

## When a real `.xlsm` (ideally with an actual, non-trivial VBA project) is
## supplied:

1. Add it here, e.g. `tests/fixtures/xlsm_roundtrip/real_vba_project.xlsm`.
2. Add a new `#[test] fn real_excel_xlsm_roundtrip()` in
   `tests/xlsx_roundtrip.rs`, mirroring the flagship test's assertions
   (edited cell round-trips; `xl/vbaProject.bin` byte-identical; every other
   original part byte-identical; content-types self-consistent) against the
   real file instead of the synthetic one.
3. This is also the point at which "does real Microsoft Excel actually open
   the round-tripped output without a repair prompt" becomes verifiable —
   something no test in this repo can check without a real Excel install
   (tracked in `ROADMAP.md`'s "no Microsoft Excel validation, at all" gap).

Not yet done — no file has been supplied as of this milestone.
